content.comment_body: Hello, I am trying to connect to my [product_name] via the Internet and upload a new program. In the Tools > Transfer > Access Control section, I connect using Dynamic DNS. When I test the connection at [url]:10002, it shows a successful connection (green lines), but after pressing OK, it prompts for a password. I am certain I did not set any password.
Try using "[product_name]" as the default password.

Are you sure you want to expose your [product_name] device to the internet without any security in place? That seems risky. Does the [product_name] web server behave differently on a local LAN compared to remote access?

Thank you for your feedback. I have an extra [product_name] base for testing, and I can access it via Dynamic DNS with the default password ([product_name]). This means someone set a password on my other [product_name]. I’ll resolve the issue by visiting the location.

It’s possible someone found your device online and changed the password remotely just for amusement. Direct connections are risky. Consider using VPN or other security options. Someone might misuse it in the future, even though I haven't heard of incidents like DDoS attacks on these devices.
Actually, it seems the default password was simply left unchanged. If no passwords are set in access control, all devices use the same default password.

To enable remote access: Connect to your [product_name] and go to Tools > Transfer > Access Control. Here, you can enable different access types (remote, web server, app). To program remotely, enable remote access and set a strong password. If no password is set, you can try using [product_name] as the password. After configuring, press APPLY in the relevant section. For local testing: 1) Download to the device, 2) Select Dynamic DNS as 'connect through', 3) Enter the IP address of your [product_name] with :8080 (e.g., 192.168.0.3:8080), 4) Follow the steps in the dialog. Connect your [product_name] to your internet router and test the Dynamic DNS connection online. Strongly recommended: set a strong password or use a VPN for remote connections. You may also need to configure port forwarding on your router (from port 8080 to your device’s IP address). Hope this helps.

It seems the user understands the procedure but overlooked the password setup, leading to these security issues. This is a common problem—if you don’t know what to look for in the manual, it’s hard to find help. Security warnings should be standard, but ease of use seems to take priority.

analysis.insight_summary: Users trying to remotely connect to [product_name] hardware via Dynamic DNS face unexpected password requests, security risks, and unclear default access behavior. The discussion emphasizes the dangers of exposing devices online without sufficient protection and highlights confusion around password management. There’s a consensus that default settings may lack proper security, potentially leaving devices vulnerable if users are unaware.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to connect and upload programs to [product_name] remotely over the Internet without being prompted for a password unless they have set one explicitly.
pain_keywords: vulnerability due to lack of security guidance
